This week's 1.145 release adds cron schedules and workspace custom agents to local automations. Recurring work, without retyping the task.

Prompts become routines. Judgment stays human.

Copilot CLI now gathers plugins, MCP servers and searchable settings in /settings. Our Tech Thursday image-batch walkthrough shows why a working connection still needs a visual review: test one image against your brief before scaling.
Follow @layer8culture if you're building with AI.

VS Code just made recurring AI work more precise. Here's a first workflow worth saving.

WHAT CHANGED
VS Code 1.145, released November 4, adds five-field cron schedules and workspace custom agents to local automations. Cloud automations don't get cron in this release.

WHAT IT DOES
You can schedule a repeatable local agent task instead of starting it manually each time.

BUILDER VALUE
Give a recurring draft a defined input, output and stopping point. That creates a routine you can inspect, not another sprawling chat.

TRY THIS WEEK
Create a workspace custom agent whose job is to summarize three approved PUBLIC sources into a dated Markdown roundup with source links. In a local automation, choose that agent and Cron. For weekday mornings, try 0 9 * * 1-5 and verify the dialog's schedule description and local time. Run it on demand once; inspect every claim and link. No inbox access, sending or publishing. Local means it depends on your local setup being available.

THE SIGNAL
AI is moving from prompts into repeatable work. On Tech Thursday, we named morning roundups and correspondence as tasks to break apart. This is a way to test the roundup idea, not a claim we already deployed this new feature.

Our content engine keeps its own boundary too: nothing publishes without a merged approval PR.

Save this for your first scheduled AI draft.

text:
AI image batches: a working connection can still produce the wrong look.

On our latest Tech Thursday walkthrough, the host showed images generated through a CLI/MCP connection, then said the quality wasn't what he wanted. He didn't claim to know whether the prompts were the problem. That's a useful distinction: observe first, diagnose second.

Use this four-part review before scaling a creative workflow:

1. CONNECT
Check which tool and model will run. Copilot CLI's new unified /settings dashboard makes plugins, MCP servers and settings easier to inspect. A successful connection proves access, not quality.

2. BRIEF
Name the subject, composition, palette and text-free areas. Give the tool a concrete job, not just a mood.

3. TEST ONE
Generate one image. Compare it with the brief. Record the specific mismatch before changing a variable; don't guess at the cause.

4. REVIEW THE BATCH
Once the test fits, scale the run. Check every output before approval. In this engine, publishing still waits for a merged human-approval PR.

The point isn't to make more images. It's to make the right ones repeatably.

Save this for your next AI image batch.
